figures.caption: FIGURE 6-33 The basic configuration of the nervous system.
figures.publisher_description: At the top of the diagram is central nervous system or C N S with brain and spinal cord. Then comes the peripheral nervous system with nerves that connect all parts of the body to the brain and motor division, which is made up of motor fibers that conduct nerve impulses from C N S to muscles and glands. The motor division is divided into two, autonomic nervous system that conducts nerve impulses from C N S to organs and glands and the somatic nervous system that conducts nerve impulses from C N S to muscles; voluntary control. Then comes the sympathetic division that activates body during emergency situations and the parasympathetic division that controls nonemergency functions. The sensory division conducts sensory information from sense organs and other internal organs to C N S through the peripheral nervous system, which has nerves that connect all parts of the body to the brain, that is, the central nervous system or C N S with brain and spinal cord.
